rationale: All four lenses and the standards audit ran cleanly with no failures or truncation, and a spec was present, but one blocking finding needs a human decision (CR-001: which layer should recover gateway keys stranded by a failed-org-fetch first connect) which forces confidence to low. Five findings are blocking: a marker/gateway-key divergence that can permanently strand secrets in Claude Desktop's config (CR-001, decision_needed), a non-transactional config/marker write pair in removeDesktopConfig (CR-002), a stable/Insiders partial-write masked as total failure in both VS Code connectors (CR-003), the spec's explicit printSummary reporting shape not adopted in disconnect-orchestrator.ts (CR-004), and missing CLI-parser-level test coverage for the three new disconnect flags (CR-005). Five other lens claims were verified against source and dismissed as non-issues (readManagedMcpState already catches the empty-marker JSON.parse failure; missing restart reminder, cross-module writeAtomically import, and sequential-await dispatch are cosmetic/non-blocking; the unsupported-platform swallow mirrors pre-existing connect behavior); zero findings were deferred.

findings.title: Marker not seeded on failed org fetch
findings.problem: writeDesktopConfig only writes the managed-MCP marker when orgFetchSucceeded is true (desktop.ts:857-860, 923-925), but it unconditionally writes the gateway keys (inferenceProvider/inferenceGatewayBaseUrl/inferenceGatewayApiKey/inferenceGatewayAuthScheme) to the config file regardless of fetch outcome (desktop.ts:899-906). If the org catalog fetch fails on a user's very first `connect --claude-desktop`, no marker file is ever created.
findings.impact: removeDesktopConfig's first check (`managedNames.length === 0`) then always short-circuits to `removed: false` for that install, so `disconnect --claude-desktop` reports 'nothing to disconnect' forever while the gateway API key and base URL remain in the Claude Desktop config on disk — a secret-retention gap the new disconnect feature was meant to close.
findings.recommendation: Needs a product decision: either always write the marker (even as an empty managed-MCP list) whenever gateway keys are written, or have removeDesktopConfig detect gateway-key presence independently of the MCP marker so a failed-fetch-then-disconnect scenario is still recoverable.

findings.title: removeDesktopConfig write/clear not transactional
findings.problem: removeDesktopConfig writes the stripped config via writeAtomically(configPath, ...) and then, as a second independent call, clears the marker via writeAtomically(statePath, ''). There is no rollback or combined transaction between the two writes.
findings.impact: If the config write succeeds but the marker clear throws (disk full, permissions change mid-run, process kill), the config is already stripped but the marker still lists the old managed names — the next disconnect run's readManagedMcpState believes managed entries still exist and re-runs reconciliation against an already-clean config, and a later connect's previouslyManagedNames union carries stale names forward.
findings.recommendation: Clear the marker before, or as part of the same failure-handling path as, the config write (e.g. write the marker first, or catch-and-retry so a partial failure leaves a consistent state), mirroring the write-ahead-then-narrow marker discipline writeDesktopConfig already uses for connect.

findings.title: Insiders-location failure masks stable-location success
findings.problem: removeVsCodeLanguageModelsConfig (vscode.ts:339-354) and removeVsCodeClaudeCodeConfig (vscode-claude-code.ts:262-296) loop over [stable, insiders]; if writeAtomically throws on the second (Insiders) iteration after the stable location already succeeded, the exception propagates out of the function, discarding the fact that removedAny was already true for the stable location.
findings.impact: disconnect-orchestrator.ts's runVscode/runVscodeClaudeCode catch the thrown error and print a flat '✗ ... — <message>' failure line even though the stable-location file was already updated on disk — the user is told disconnect failed when it partially succeeded, and a re-run masks this further because the stable location now short-circuits as already-clean.
findings.recommendation: Wrap each loop iteration's read/filter/write in its own try/catch, accumulate per-location errors, and still return removed: true (with an error summary) when at least one location succeeded, in both vscode.ts and vscode-claude-code.ts.

findings.title: disconnect-orchestrator doesn't adopt printSummary shape
findings.problem: spec.md explicitly requires disconnect-orchestrator.ts to 'adopt connect-orchestrator.ts's TargetResult/printSummary convention rather than keep disconnect's ad hoc single-target prints' (spec.md:104-108). The diff reuses the TargetResult interface and collects results into an array (disconnect-orchestrator.ts:134), but never defines or calls a printSummary() function — each target's line is still printed inline inside its own runClaudeDesktop/runVscode/runVscodeClaudeCode/runCodexDesktop function.
findings.impact: Per-target success/failure information is emitted, but the specific reporting convention the spec names as the required pattern — a consolidated summary block after all targets run, matching connect's output shape — was not implemented, leaving disconnect's output inconsistent with connect's and with what the spec calls out as the intended shape.
findings.recommendation: Add a printSummary(results: TargetResult[]) function mirroring connect-orchestrator.ts's, move the inline per-target print statements out of the run* functions (or keep them silent and rely on printSummary), and call printSummary(results) at the end of disconnectTargets.

findings.title: No CLI-parser-level test for new disconnect flags
findings.problem: index.ts wires --claude-desktop/--vscode/--vscode-claude-code on the disconnect command (lines 319-321, 331-334) the same way --codex-desktop already is, but connect-wiring.test.ts only exercises the disconnect command's Commander parsing end-to-end for --codex-desktop (lines 205-211); the three new flags are only covered by disconnect-orchestrator.test.ts calling disconnectTargets({targets:{...}}) directly, bypassing option parsing entirely.
findings.impact: If any of the three new option strings and their destructured opts.* property names ever drift (rename, kebab-case typo), 'codemie proxy disconnect --claude-desktop' (etc.) would silently fall through to the no-target path and do nothing, and no existing test would catch it.
findings.recommendation: Add parseAsync-based tests for --claude-desktop, --vscode, and --vscode-claude-code on the disconnect command, mirroring the existing --codex-desktop test at connect-wiring.test.ts:205-211.
